intent: The visible caption that names what its progress bar is the progress of.
typical_uses: The caption beside the bar, composed as a child of Progress

dont_use_when.situation: A caption for anything that is not a progress bar

invariants.text: A ProgressLabel registers its id with the root, which wires it into the progressbar's `aria-labelledby`, so the caption's text becomes the bar's accessible name; the span itself renders `role="presentation"` and nothing announces it as a separate element.

anti_patterns.dont: Point a `<label htmlFor>` at the bar's id
anti_patterns.do_instead: Compose this ProgressLabel into the root - a `<label>` element cannot name a div, and the root wires `aria-labelledby` only from a ProgressLabel's registered id

a11y.by: the primitive's Progress.Label, which registers its id with the root for `aria-labelledby` and renders role="presentation" (verified in the @base-ui/react/progress source); progress.test.tsx asserts the label's span and its text

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the label's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.states: style accepts a function of the label's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (status). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through progress.module.css, not through this.

good.title: A caption composed inside the wrapper

bad.title: A label with no progress root around it
bad.why: The label registers its id with the nearest progress root through React context and throws when there is none.
